title: Подозрительно добрый Шеф  (A Suspiciously Kind Chef)

segments.t: Huddled together in the kitchen, the cooks try to figure out why Chef Barinov is suddenly so polite, sober, and forgiving this morning. Since Spartak lost and the Chef has not touched a drop of alcohol, Fedya convinces the team that something serious must be wrong.
Слушайте, что-то шеф какой-то сегодня слишком добрый.
Просто человек нажрался с утра, и все.
Ну, есть у меня один знакомый, он рассказывал.
Now let's go back through the conversation line by line.
'We are just friends.' Chef Viktor brings out the contrast between 'we' and 'just' in a few short words. Max answers right away.
'Nothing at all.' The meaning hinges on 'yes' working together with 'nothing' in spoken Russian.
'Well, friendship is a wonderful thing.' Notice how Russian expresses 'come on' and 'wonderful' with crisp inflection rather than helper words.
Слушайте, что-то шеф какой-то сегодня слишком добрый.
'Listen, the Chef is being way too kind today.' Max anchors the line on 'listen', while 'good' completes the thought. Chef Viktor answers right away.
'That does not bode well.' In Russian, the idea of 'there you go' flows naturally into 'good' without extra filler words.
'Maybe Spartak won?' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'maybe' and finishing on 'won'.
'No, it looks like they lost.' The '-l' ending on the verb meaning 'lost' places the action in the masculine past tense. Max answers right away.
Просто человек нажрался с утра, и все.
'The man simply got wasted first thing in the morning, that is all.' Notice the reflexive suffix on the verb meaning 'get hammered', turning the action back on the subject.
'No, he seemed completely sober.' Chef Viktor brings out the contrast between 'there is no' and 'seemingly' in a few short words.
'Something else is going on here.' The meaning hinges on 'here' working together with 'something else' in spoken Russian. Chef Viktor answers right away.
'How do you even know about that?' In Russian, the idea of 'you' flows naturally into 'at all' without extra filler words.
Ну, есть у меня один знакомый, он рассказывал.
'Well, I have an acquaintance who told me all about it.' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'come on' before landing on 'to tell'.
'Anyway, look here.' In Russian, the idea of 'in short' flows naturally into 'look' without extra filler words. Alright, let's hear the whole conversation once more from start to finish.
Слушайте, что-то шеф какой-то сегодня слишком добрый.
Просто человек нажрался с утра, и все.
Ну, есть у меня один знакомый, он рассказывал.
